questions.stem:
A particle $P$ of weight $W$ newtons is attached to one end of a light inextensible string. The other end of the string is attached to a fixed point $O$. A horizontal force of magnitude 5 N is applied to $P$. The particle $P$ is in equilibrium with the string taut and with $OP$ making an angle of $25°$ to the downward vertical, as shown in Figure 1.

Find

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Resolving horizontally: $5 = T\cos 65°$ M1A1
$T = 12, 11.8,$ or better (N) A1

First M1 for resolving horizontally with correct no. of terms and $T$ term resolved. First A1 for a correct equation in $T$ only. Second A1 for 12 (N) or 11.8 (N) or better.
N.B. The M1 is for a complete method to find the tension so where two resolution equations, neither horizontal, are used, the usual criteria for the M mark must be applied to both equations and the first A1 is for a correct equation in $T$ only (i.e. $W$ eliminated correctly)
Alternatives:
Lami's Theorem: $\frac{T}{\sin 90°} = \frac{5}{\sin 155°}$ (same equation as resolution) M1A1

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) Resolving vertically: $W = T\cos 25°$ M1A1
$= 11.8\cos 25° = 11, 10.7$ or better (N) A1

First M1 for resolving vertically with correct no. of terms and $T$ (does not need to be substituted) term resolved. First A1 for a correct equation in $T$ only. Second A1 for 11 (N), 10.7 (N) or better.
Alternatives:
Triangle of forces: $W = 5\tan 65°$ M1A1
Lami's Theorem: $\frac{T}{\sin 90°} = \frac{W}{\sin 115°}$ M1A1
Or Resolution in another direction e.g. along the string M1 (usual criteria) A1 for a correct equation.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $(4\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})+(2\mathbf{i}+q\mathbf{j}) = (6\mathbf{i}+(q-2)\mathbf{j})$ M1A1
$6 = 2(q-2)$ ratio 2:1 DM1
$q = 5$ A1

First A1 for $(6\mathbf{i}+(q-2)\mathbf{j})$ (seen or implied)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
At time $t=0$, $P$ is moving with velocity $(-2\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$ m s$^{-1}$.

(b) Find the speed of $P$ at time $t=2$ seconds.
(6)

It moves at constant speed $V$ m s$^{-1}$ for the next 30 seconds, then moves with constant deceleration $\frac{1}{2}$ m s$^{-2}$ until it has speed 8 m s$^{-1}$. It moves at speed 8 m s$^{-1}$ for the next 15 seconds and then moves with constant deceleration $\frac{1}{3}$ m s$^{-2}$ until it comes to rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Sketch, in the space below, a speed-time graph for this journey.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:

Second B1 for shape of graph for $t>50$
Third B1 for $V, 8, 15, 20, 30$ appropriately used

parts.label: b
parts.text:
In the first 20 seconds of this journey the car travels 140 m.

Find

(b) the value of $V$,
(2)

$V=14$ A1

questions.stem: At time $t=0$, a particle is projected vertically upwards with speed $u$ from a point $A$. The particle moves freely under gravity. At time $T$ the particle is at its maximum height $H$ above $A$.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
Max ht $v=0$. $v=u-gt \Rightarrow T=\frac{u}{g}$ M1A1

M1 for use of suvat to obtain an equation in $T, u$ and $g$ only.
A1 for $T=u/g$ correctly obtained.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- e.g. in (a), using $v = u + at$, either $0 = u - gT$ or $u = 0 + gT$

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
Max ht $H=ut+\frac{1}{2}at^2 = \frac{u^2}{g}-\frac{u^2}{2g} = \frac{u^2}{2g}$ *Given answer* M1A1
Or use of $v^2=u^2+2as$

M1 for use of suvat to obtain an equation in $H, u$ and $g$ only.
A1 for $H=u^2/2g$ correctly obtained (given answer)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The point $A$ is at a height $3H$ above the ground.

(c) Find, in terms of $T$, the total time from the instant of projection to the instant when the particle hits the ground.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
$-3\times\frac{u^2}{2g} = ut-\frac{1}{2}gt^2$ M1
$-3u^2 = 2ugt-g^2t^2$
$g^2t^2-2ugt-3u^2=0$, $gt=\frac{2u\pm\sqrt{4u^2+12u^2}}{2}$ DM1A1
$t=\frac{3u}{g}=3T$ A1

Alternative:
$-4H=-\frac{1}{2}gt^2$ M1
Total time $=T+\sqrt{\frac{8H}{g}}=T+\sqrt{\frac{8u^2}{2g^2}}$ DM1A1
$=T+2T=3T$ A1

In this question, condone sign errors in a suvat equation for the M mark, but a missing term is M0 or an incorrect term is M0. An incorrect suvat formula is M0. Allow use of symmetry of motion.
Watch out for $t/T$ confusion (N.B. if only $T$'s used, M0DM0)

either: $3H=-ut+\frac{1}{2}gt^2$

or: $v^2=u^2+6gH$ and $v=-u+gt$, with $v$ eliminated

First A1 for any correct expression for the total time in terms of $u,g,H$ or $T$.

questions.stem:
A particle $P$ of mass 2.7 kg lies on a rough plane inclined at $40°$ to the horizontal. The particle is held in equilibrium by a force of magnitude 15 N acting at an angle of $50°$ to the plane, as shown in Figure 4. The force acts in a vertical plane containing a line of greatest slope of the plane. The particle is in equilibrium and is on the point of sliding down the plane.

Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the magnitude of the normal reaction of the plane on $P$,
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Perpendicular to the slope: $R=2.7g\cos 40+15\cos 40$ M1A2
$=31.8$ (N) or 32 (N) A1

First M1 for resolving perpendicular to the slope, with correct no. of terms, and both the 2.7g and 15 terms resolved.
First A2 for a correct equation; -1 each error.
Third A1 for 32 (N) or 31.8 (N)
N.B. Only penalise over- or under-accuracy after using $g=9.8$, (or use of $g=9.81$), once in whole question.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
Parallel to the slope: $F=2.7g\sin 40-15\cos 50$ $(F=7.366..)$ M1A2
Use of $F=\mu R$ M1
$\mu = \frac{2.7g\sin 40-15\cos 50}{R} = 0.23$ or $0.232$ A1

First M1 for resolving parallel to the slope, with correct no. of terms, and both the 2.7g and 15 terms resolved.
First A2 for a correct equation; -1 each error.
Second M1 for use of $F=\mu R$
Third A1 for 0.23 or 0.232

parts.label: c

(4)

$F_{max}=0.232\times 2.7\times g\times\cos 40° = 4.7...$ (N) M1A1
$17.0>4.70$ so the particle moves A1

B1 for component of weight down the plane $2.7g\sin 40°$ (17 or better)
